authority.decision_basis: The incumbent is spread across 246 Rust files and 558 exact source lines, owns production Condvar and visible guard semantics, and saves four package versions in 48 of 52 canonical graph cells. A safe std-backed replacement remains plausible, but the required 1/8/32/64-core Linux and Apple throughput, p50/p95/p99/p999, fairness, starvation, cancellation-adjacent, allocation, RSS, compile-time, binary-size, and stable-lane comparison receipts do not exist. Missing parity evidence cannot authorize implementation or cutover.

source_census.algorithm: Over the clean baseline tree, recursively inspect Rust files under benches, examples, fuzz, src, and tests; exclude tests/oslock_inventory_gate_contract.rs; emit one UTF-8 record path:text for every line containing the dependency token, preserving duplicate records; sort records bytewise; terminate every record with LF; hash the complete stream with SHA-256. Line numbers are intentionally excluded so unrelated insertions cannot invalidate an unchanged dependency use.

semantic_matrix.finding: parking_lot is non-poisoning. The proposed safe std backend must recover poisoned guards internally and keep that policy explicit rather than leaking std LockResult across existing call sites.
RAII guards release the incumbent lock during unwind; a replacement must preserve unlock while applying the explicit poison-recovery policy.
Recursive acquisition is not a supported contract and may deadlock. Call-site lock-order and reentrancy audits are incomplete.
semantic_matrix.route: lock-order inventory and deterministic deadlock fixtures

semantic_matrix.finding: try_lock, try_read, and try_write behavior is used directly and through owned Asupersync wrappers.
Production blocking-pool Condvar wait_for is load-bearing. No direct timed Mutex/RwLock acquisition contract was found.
No retained incumbent-versus-candidate fairness distribution or starvation bound exists at 1/8/32/64 cores.
Some local orders are documented, including watch send_lock before value, but there is no complete 246-file order graph.
parking_lot primitives are synchronous and not cancellation-aware. Asupersync async wrappers own waiter teardown and prohibit guards across await, but direct call sites still require review.
Asupersync owns borrowed and owned mapped-guard APIs in src/sync/mutex.rs; direct parking_lot mapped guards are absent.
Blocking-pool shutdown and DNS discovery coalescing depend on wait, wait_for, notify_one, and notify_all.
semantic_matrix.route: production Condvar parity and quiescence fixtures

semantic_matrix.finding: The incumbent compiles on the audited stable lane. Any safe std wrapper must preserve that lane before a cutover decision.
Blocking-pool notify-all shutdown paths exist, but no replacement-side quiescence receipt exists.
ContendedMutex exposes optional wait and hold metrics using std::sync, but that is not a complete baseline for direct parking_lot call sites.
Only a safe std-backed owned wrapper is admissible by default. A raw futex or parking protocol is separately ALGORITHMIC-UNSAFE and prohibited without a complete exception record.

marginal_graph.no_claim: The ledger proves graph deltas only. Unknown marginal native status is not evidence of native code presence or absence, and package removal does not prove runtime parity or a favorable performance trade.

gaps.finding: The full 1/8/32/64-core Linux and Apple performance matrix is absent.
p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, fairness, and starvation receipts are absent.
Allocation, RSS, compile-time, and binary-size comparisons are absent.
There is no complete lock-order and recursive-acquisition audit across the 246-file surface.
Production Condvar predicate, timeout, shutdown, and spurious-wakeup parity has no candidate receipt.
Direct public and crate-visible parking_lot guard/type signatures have no approved migration contract.
Cancellation-adjacent direct lock use and no-await-with-guard coverage are incomplete.
A candidate safe std wrapper does not exist, so stable-lane, poisoning, mapping, and owned-guard parity cannot be measured.

The clean-HEAD focused incumbent sync suite failed mutex_queued_waiter_sees_poison_after_holder_panics after 614 passes, while the same test passed alone. Its fixed 10 ms and 50 ms sleeps leave suite-order or load sensitivity unresolved.

reconsideration_triggers.condition: A named-host 1/8/32/64-core comparison covers throughput, p50/p95/p99/p999, fairness, starvation, allocation, RSS, compile time, and binary size and meets an owner-approved budget.
A safe std-backed candidate passes poison, panic, try, Condvar, mapping, lock-order, cancellation-adjacent, shutdown, quiescence, and stable-lane contracts.
A supported-platform production defect is attributable to the incumbent and cannot be repaired upstream or while retaining it.
An applicable advisory, unsoundness report, or maintenance-abandonment record materially changes incumbent risk.
A fresh canonical marginal ledger proves an owner-approved package, build-script, native-code, or supply-chain budget violation.

decision.required_next_action: Retain the incumbent. Reopen implementation only through a new owner-reviewed gate after the named correctness and performance evidence exists.
decision.rollback: No production source, manifest, or lockfile change is authorized or required by this terminal inventory.

no_claim_boundaries: This inventory does not prove release readiness, broad workspace health, or performance equivalence.
The focused sync test receipt covers incumbent sync unit tests only; it does not cover all 246 files, all targets, all features, or a candidate replacement.
The source census proves exact dependency-token coverage at one revision; it does not prove that every lock is correctly ordered or cancellation-safe.
The marginal ledger proves package-graph deltas only and does not prove native-code presence, runtime benefit, or acceptable engineering cost.

DEFER is terminal success for this gate. This artifact does not authorize implementing a wrapper, migrating call sites, removing parking_lot, editing Cargo manifests, or unblocking implementation children.
No local Cargo fallback, peer build cancellation, file deletion, branch creation, worktree creation, or destructive cleanup is authorized.
